one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is the September-quarter (FQ1'27) report. It is estimated for about Oct 21-22, 2026 (aggregators; Lam reported the Sep-2025 quarter on Oct 22, 2025). Lam has not announced the date: as of Sep 30 there is no 8-K or IR notice, and the latest EDGAR filings are the Sep 24 proxy and Form 4/144s. The guide was $8.10B +/- $0.4B revenue, 52% GM and $2.15 EPS, and management's tone at Citi TMT (Sep 9: WFE in the low $150Bs, 'undersupplying demand') makes a beat with a higher December guide likely. But the stock has already bounced ~20% from the $269 closes on Sep 16-17 (it closed $273.49 on Sep 14 after the AI 'pacing' call, not $279 as I had it), and it trades ~34x FY27 EPS, so the reaction is close to a coin flip with fat tails. TSMC and ASML report in mid-October and AI-capex headlines can move it either way. I keep a lognormal centred slightly above spot (~$327) with monthly sigma ~18.5% (65%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sept 2027 ~$12.0, built on FY28 S&P Global consensus of $11.74, x 26x = $312, 60%) and FCF yield (NTM FCF ~$13.7B at 3.6% + ~$6B net cash over 1.24B shares = $312, 40%) -> ~$312 at Sept 2027.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Sept 2027 ~$12.0 (FY28 Jun-28 consensus $11.74 rolled forward one quarter) x 26x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P Global via StockAnalysis on Sep 30. Cross-check: the Sept-26 quarter guide of $2.15 +/- 0.15 on 1.255B shares (source 1) and a rising run-rate give ~$9.5.

I now use consensus instead of my round-1 $11.00. SEMI's independent July 2026 view (WFE +21.8% in 2027, +14.1% in 2028; DRAM equipment +27%, NAND +31% in 2027) supports ~+23% EPS growth from $9.51, because Lam is memory-weighted. The mid-teens tax step-up (source 4) is already in consensus. I found no primary-source reason to cut it.
FY28 $11.74, with one quarter rolled into FY29 at ~10% annualized growth (SEMI 2028 WFE +14.1%, slowing) = ~$12.0.

Today $324.5 is ~34x FY27 / ~27.6x FY28 consensus. By Sept 2027 the market will be discounting CY2028-29. SEMI still sees 2028 growth, but it slows from ~22% to ~14%, and semicap usually de-rates as growth decelerates toward a peak. So 26x: below today's ~28x on the next-year number, above the ~20x mid-cycle. I raised it from 27x on FY28 in round 1 to 26x on a later, larger NTM base, which is about the same multiple once the base is rolled forward.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Sept 2027 ~$13.7B / 3.6% yield = $381B + ~$6B net cash = $387B / 1.24B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 conversion was held down by the capex step-up (Malaysia, a >$3B lab-network plan in Tualatin) and by working capital (deferred revenue $2.43B, Japan shipments awaiting acceptance). As revenue grows ~18%/yr, inventory and receivables build keeps conversion somewhat below 100%. Net: ~92%, giving ~$13.7B.

June-26 cash $5.6B minus debt $3.73B = ~$1.9B. Add ~12 months of FCF (~$11-12B) and subtract dividends (~$1.65B at $0.33/qtr) and buybacks (~$6B; the Q4 FY26 pace of $246M was unusually low versus ~$1.4B/qtr earlier).
Sept-26 quarter guide of 1.255B; FY26 repurchases ~23M shares; at $300+ prices, assume ~1% net reduction.
Today ~2.8% on depressed FY26 FCF and ~3.4% on FY27E. Peak-cycle semicap is normally 4-5%. 3.6% reflects decelerating but still growing WFE in 2028 (SEMI) and consistency with the 26x P/E leg.

bear.story: AI-capex pacing (the Sept-2026 Amodei 'slow the pace' call, echoed by other labs) turns into 2H-2027 order push-outs, memory pricing rolls over, or a new China rule (MATCH Act floor vote) lands. The market then prices a 2028 WFE decline against SEMI's +14%. NTM EPS ~$10 at ~18x = ~$180.

base.story: CY2027 WFE grows ~20% (SEMI ~$175B), cleanroom-constrained. Lam outgrows WFE on NAND conversions and DRAM, GM moves to 53-54%, FY28 EPS ~$11.7 in line with consensus. By Sept 2027 the multiple de-rates to ~26-27x NTM (~$12) as 2028 growth slows to low-teens.

bull.story: Cleanrooms open faster, DRAM/HBM and NAND adds beat SEMI's +27%/+31%, and 2028 looks like another 15%+ year. NTM EPS ~$13.5-14 at ~34-35x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$205 (about -37%, ~17.5x FY28 consensus of $11.74 and ~21.5x FY27's $9.51; under the July $252 capitulation close and the Sept $269 closes) the market would be pricing an actual 2027-28 WFE decline rather than a de-rating. That would contradict SEMI's +22%/+14% path and management's 'cleanroom-constrained through 2027' view, and most likely means AI-capex pushouts or memory price roll-over hitting orders, or a major new export-control action.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established two facts I had missed. (1) FY28 consensus EPS is $11.74 (S&P Global, re-verified on StockAnalysis Sep 30), not the ~$11.00 I assumed. (2) SEMI's July 14, 2026 mid-year forecast (re-verified) sees WFE +21.8% in 2027 and +14.1% in 2028 to $200B, with DRAM/NAND equipment +27%/+31% in 2027, well above my 10-15% CY27 growth. I found no primary-source reason to haircut consensus, so I adopted it. My disagreement remains the multiple: at $324.5 the stock is ~27.6x FY28 consensus, and in Sept 2027 the market will value it on CY28-29, when growth slows to ~14%. Semicap typically de-rates into deceleration, so I use 26x on ~$12 NTM EPS = $312, with an FCF-yield cross-check at $312. Fair value moved $305 -> $312, still slightly below spot. The ladder is a mixture: 92% lognormal (median $330, sigma 0.50, below the 65% realized vol because part of that is event noise that mean-reverts over a year) plus 8% downturn (median $195, sigma 0.35). I cut the downturn weight from 12% because SEMI forecasts no 2028 decline, so a full downturn is a tail rather than a base-rate default; I kept 8% because semicap has historically priced peaks early and the Sept-14 episode showed how fast sentiment can crack. The result is median ~$315, P(>=spot) ~0.48, mean ~$340, consistent with 22/53/25 scenarios at $180/$320/$480. Lam has not confirmed the report date (EDGAR shows no 8-K since Aug 27). Research this round was limited to 3 checks (EDGAR index, StockAnalysis, SEMI release).
